title: Token Surge Microcalibrator: p95 drift sentinel & tokens/sec micro-harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build and maintain a compact, repeatable microbenchmark harness (the Token Surge Microcalibrator) that reliably measures tokens/sec and tail latency (p95/p99) for core serving models across hardware variants and kernel configs. The harness must run in CI, produce artifactable metrics and artifacts (histograms, per-run golden traces), and support automated regression detection with configurable sensitivity.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic harness that runs in < 10 minutes for core model set and emits tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, token distribution histograms, and per-step timings.
Automated regression detector that raises a GitHub PR check failure when tokens/sec drop > 7% relative to the golden baseline OR p95 increases > 15% with >= 95% confidence (configurable thresholds).
CI job (gha) that runs on model rollouts and nightly cadence, writes metric artifacts to S3 (s3://redwood-bench/token-surge/) and exposes summary to Prometheus/Grafana.
Dashboard tile + alert rule created (alert to #infra-bench) with actionable runbook.
Runnable locally via dockerized harness and documented in the runtime-performance README with example commands and sample payloads.
tasks: Design harness runner API (Go) with pluggable sampler and workload profiles
Implement cold vs warm KV scenarios and sequence-length cohorts (8/64/512)
Add jitter + burst injection harness to simulate microbursts and sustained streams
Integrate artifact uploads to S3 and attach run metadata (git sha, model id, machine type)
Add statistical regression detector (EWMA + bootstrap CI) and GitHub check integration
Dockerize harness and add GitHub Actions workflow (token-surge/nightly + on-model-rollout)
Create Grafana dashboard panels and alerting rule with playbook
Run golden baseline sweep on all core models and save baseline snapshots
notes: 2026-02-20 — Triage: prioritized after perf review; assigned to Marco Nguyen. Decided to favor small deterministic workloads to keep CI cost low.

2026-02-26 — Design review: agreed on three sequence cohorts and explicit KV cold/warm toggles. Chose Go for runner to match runtime telemetry tooling. Follow-up: sketch GitHub check contract and artifact schema.

2026-03-03 — Implementation: basic runner working (local). Measured initial baselines on g4dn and a40; see s3 artifacts. Observed 4–9% variance across identical runs; will add EWMA smoothing and 5-run aggregation.
2026-03-07 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7423 — contains Dockerfile, harness runner, and initial CI workflow. Requesting review from @sylvia-chen and @eric-taylor.

2026-03-10 — CI smoke: nightly run green, but one model (rwd-13b-quant) had p95 +18% on a40 after kernel change; regression detector triggered and created an incident ticket (ENG-214800) for kernel rollback investigation. Logged artifacts and profiler snapshots to S3.
Next steps: finalize GitHub check failure message with remediation links, add per-host variance tracking, and run a 72-hour stability sweep to tighten thresholds.
